title: Other composers in the band
summary: Everyone but the guitarist contributed; he mentions Carney, Hodges, Freddie Jenkins, Rockin' in Rhythm credit and his $15 check again.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: How about other members of the band? Who were some of the other composers in the band?

Well, let me see -- Harry Carney, of course Johnny. And Barney, Tricky -- that was Tricky Sam, Cootie and most everybody did something. Freddy Jenkins -- he wrote several tunes before he had to leave. And I've never heard anything about what happened to them so I don't know, but everybody, with the exception of the guitar player, used to contribute in the musical side of the aggregation.
Well, he sang a little bit you know. He sang quite a bit. Everybody backed up what was going on to the other members.
Uh-huh. Now what did Harry write?

Oh, he -- there again I don't remember the names, but the solos, concertos, and things like that he wrote his part or contributed in his part. And then when he -- he would take the insertions of different tunes. And he wrote -- anytime you had an open space for you -- he wrote -- you put that together.
You were a Composer. He wrote the part. Now I think Harry has composer credits -- co-credit on "Rockin in Rhythm" but
I think it was Barney that told me that he didn't write it. That someone Duke just decided to give him.
That was before my time. I'm a young fellow -- one of the young members.
I think you mentioned to me, off the tape, that you got, you and Otto Hardwick each got $15.00 for your contribution to --
"Sophisticated Lady" -- yes I got a check for $15.00. Of course in those days it was -- $15.00 was worth just about $23.00, so it was something good.
